recommended_paths:
Keep OutboundService.finalProviderFence as the common orchestrator. Give it the actual persisted selectedContext, captured recipientRef, operation policy inputs, original dispatch deadline, captured credential expiry and an optional paired human-actor fence. Introduce a small internal ActorDispatchFence interface: validateInTransaction(tx: Prisma.TransactionClient): Promise<boolean>; isSessionCurrent(now: number): boolean. Require the complete pair for BFF dispatch and initial human sends; preserve existing PUBLIC/BOT eligibility and local accepted-fact recovery behavior.

Open one short ReadCommitted transaction in finalProviderFence. Add a narrow DispatchAdmissionService.pinContextForFinalDispatch(tx, context, recipientRef): Promise<boolean> that reuses the existing qualified-address and lock helpers. Acquire the provider identity, qualified peer and conversation protection in the established order, then reuse validateDispatchContext and resolver.validateOperationContextInTransaction with the persisted tuple and captured recipient. Inspect and evaluate the existing abstract policy using that same transaction. Invoke the existing actor/grant callback last, through the same transaction. Return only authorization and expiry facts; await transaction completion, then synchronously check the signed session, original dispatch deadline, window edge and strict 60-second credential margin. Provider HTTP remains outside the transaction. Remove the final fence's PrismaService-to-TransactionClient cast; contextBeforeDispatch and earlier adapter checks may remain preliminary observations but cannot supply the decisive authorization.

The smallest cohesive source set is outbound.service.ts, dispatch-admission.service.ts, conversations.service.ts, initial-message.service.ts and conversations.controller.ts, plus a bounded nonwaiting adaptation in the existing admitted contact-identity.ts helper if required to reuse its exact peer-lock key. Reuse the resolver validator and policy APIs without introducing another resolver, sender or policy framework. Tests belong in instagram-cp3-authorization-fences.e2e-spec.ts; helpers.ts needs changes only for synthetic boundary recording or reusable native barriers. No SessionService, AccessService, protected middleware, concrete provider-client, schema, configuration or public-route change is proposed.

A single SQL statement could provide a coherent statement snapshot in principle. It is not the simpler faithful implementation with these existing interfaces: it would duplicate resolver validation, actor authorization and origin-specific policy SQL, or require a new composition mechanism. Repeated alternating reads cannot establish coherence. Prefer reuse through the short transaction, accepting its additional round trips and fail-closed contention instead of consolidating unrelated owners into a large final-read query.
exact_next_step: Record reviewer resolutions in the governing TODO using the machine-checkable resolution table or equivalent gate ledger, then extract the derived resolution packet and decide whether another bounded review pass is still required.

findings.title: The transaction adds a COMMIT await after the current signed-session check
findings.rationale: The current callback synchronously verifies the signed session after its raw actor query. Wrapping that callback in an interactive transaction introduces a later awaited transaction completion. A session can expire during that interval even though the grant remains pinned and the original dispatch deadline is still live. Checking only the captured operation deadline would regress the existing session fence. This is a required constraint on the proposed repair, not a request to change the protected session implementation.
findings.suggested_action: Construct ActorDispatchFence in ConversationsController from the captured server-side cookie and verified request identity. Reuse currentActorHasGrant for validateInTransaction. Implement isSessionCurrent(now) with the existing SessionService.verificar(cookie, now), matching uid, iat and exp to the captured signed claims and explicitly requiring exp > now. Pass the paired fence through ConversationsService and InitialMessageService to both ordinary and initial dispatch. Immediately after await prisma.$transaction(...), obtain now and synchronously require the session check, now < original dispatchDeadlineAt, now < any windowExpiresAt, and now + 60000 < any credentialExpiresAt. Fail closed on invalid clock facts. Do not perform another database, policy or actor await afterward. Retain the existing callback's checks inside the transaction as well. Add a delegated observation barrier after the in-transaction actor check has returned true but before transaction completion, expire the real signed synthetic session while the immutable dispatch deadline remains live, and require zero provider POSTs. Keep a matched live-session control through the same barrier.

findings.title: The decisive provider, policy and actor observation must share protected transaction state
findings.rationale: The current contextBeforeDispatch, policy.inspect and actor callback are separate awaited observations. Successful reauthorization can replace the encrypted active credential after the provider read, while the later actor read remains valid. The existing transaction validator already protects BU, channel and credential rows, but explicitly assumes the caller has established the identity protection; merely placing the current finalProviderFence body inside a transaction is therefore insufficient. ReadCommitted alone also does not make successive queries one snapshot. IG-ARCH-R1-01 and DOD-03 require the captured current tuple and current authorization to agree before dispatch.
findings.suggested_action: Use the recommended final transaction with exact, bounded protection. Acquire provider_resource_identities FOR SHARE NOWAIT for the captured identity and binding; acquire the existing qualified-peer lock using its canonical key and a nonwaiting acquisition; then pin the exact conversation FOR SHARE NOWAIT and verify its BU/contact association. Continue with the existing validator's BU, channel and credential FOR SHARE NOWAIT pins, followed by policy inspection/evaluation and the existing actor query's user/grant/BU share pins. Preserve provider→qualified peer→conversation order; the later NOWAIT acquisitions must never wait while holding that prefix. Immutable route, peer and business associations remain governed by the existing database invariants. The conversation/peer protection must conflict with the canonical acceptance writers, keeping the inspected policy facts stable through the actor await. Provider and credential pins retain the validated tuple; actor pins retain the observed grant, user and tenant facts through database commit. Treat a missing row, failed peer acquisition, 55P03 or unconfirmed transaction completion as an unsuccessful pre-HTTP authorization. Roll back before projecting the existing BLOCKED/CHANNEL_CONTEXT_CHANGED result, and use existing same-owner settlement rules. Do not add automatic retries, extend deadlines, lock every connection in a BU or retain locks during HTTP. Native tests must verify the actual conflicting rows and independent-account behavior. This is bounded extra work on dispatch; no measured latency improvement or preserved performance budget can yet be claimed.

findings.title: Causal proof must distinguish mutation-first rejection from authorization-first serialization
findings.rationale: API45's six authorization cases mutate grants or session time, not the provider lifecycle in A46. Its credential-version ACK case is metadata-only and occurs after POST. The current helper pauses after the delegated context read, which exposes a real defect because policy and actor awaits still follow. Reusing a post-read pause after a repaired coherent observation and demanding that every later lifecycle change cancel dispatch would manufacture a different requirement. Conversely, moving the hook without retaining an unconditional mutation-first zero-POST control would weaken the proof.
findings.suggested_action:
Before product repair, append and execute causal tests against the frozen API45 production bytes. Hold the existing vulnerable gap after claim/provider read while the actor remains live. Complete real Instagram REAUTHORIZE through create, callback and confirm with a different synthetic long-lived token and the same verified account. Prove the active version increased, encrypted credential material was replaced and the normal credential resolver decrypts the replacement; retain channel, resource, ownership and receipt assertions. Separately invoke the actual existing ChannelsService.desconectar lifecycle for WhatsApp, covering initial and ordinary dispatch. Confirm each lifecycle mutation committed before releasing the old gap. The required zero-message-POST assertion must fail specifically because the old sender dispatches, not because setup failed or timed out.

For GREEN, retain two explicit schedules. In mutation-first cases, pause after the durable claim but before decisive provider protection, complete reauthorization or disconnect, then resume and require the existing 409 BLOCKED result and zero message POSTs. In authorization-first cases, pause within the final transaction after provider protection and before completion, start the same real lifecycle operation, and use PostgreSQL blocker evidence to prove it waits on the captured protected rows. Release the sender without awaiting the blocked mutation inside the barrier. Assert the resulting serialization and exactly one permitted captured-account/peer POST when all synchronous time checks remain valid. Control ACK ordering and assert its specific existing acceptance outcome, rather than accepting arbitrary statuses. Document that the old post-read hook becomes a serialization observation when protected; this is an observation-hook adaptation, not removal of the zero-POST requirement before authorization.

Preserve all actual grant/session negative and live controls, original deadlines, same-account and independent-account lock thresholds, formatted WhatsApp scope assertions, native P2002 count three and no-redispatch recovery assertions. Record account, peer and synthetic credential selection at the HTTP fake where needed; do not mock resolver results, Prisma transactions, lifecycle mutation or policy decisions. Capture RED and GREEN receipts separately, freeze the repaired candidate and run the affected native cases plus the complete canonical API regression. Remaining ALL/browser/performance gates retain their existing scope.

findings.title: Define local authorization serialization without claiming atomic provider effects
findings.rationale: With all relevant protection held, completion of the final in-transaction authorization checks provides a coherent local ordering point, conditional on successful transaction completion and the subsequent synchronous session/time checks. The locks persist through database commit, not through delivery of the COMMIT acknowledgement or the external request. A lifecycle mutation may therefore commit after authorization and before the HTTP fake observes POST. Preventing that interval would require a different contract, such as retaining coordination across network I/O, which the approved architecture prohibits.
findings.suggested_action: State the acceptance interpretation explicitly: a mutation committed before decisive protection must be observed and prevent POST; a concurrent mutation blocked by the final observation is ordered after that authorization. After commit, synchronously enforce session, deadline, window and credential-margin expiry, then initiate provider I/O without additional local asynchronous authorization work. Do not claim that DB authorization and the external effect are atomic. A later lifecycle change must retain the original captured account/peer and the existing ACCEPTED, ACCEPTED_LOCAL_INCOMPLETE or UNKNOWN handling as applicable; it cannot erase a known ACK, substitute current credentials into historical validation or authorize redispatch. Keep strict V1 local-only recovery and the common acceptance owner unchanged. This interpretation preserves the approved last-local-observation contract; requiring cancellation of every mutation after that point would change WHAT and must return for renewed approval.
